did_you_know.text: Did you know? Jeremiah was the son of Hilkiah, from a priestly family, and came from Anathoth in the land of Benjamin.
Did you know? Jeremiah began prophesying in the days of Josiah king of Judah, in the thirteenth year of his reign.

Did you know? According to the opening of the book, Jeremiah’s prophetic ministry continued from the days of Josiah through the reign of Jehoiakim and into the eleventh year of Zedekiah, up to the exile of Jerusalem in the fifth month.
Did you know? The LORD told Jeremiah that He knew him, set him apart, and appointed him as a prophet to the nations before he was born.
Did you know? Jeremiah was apprehensive about his calling and said that he was young and did not know how to speak, but the LORD commanded him not to use his age as a reason to avoid the mission.

Did you know? In a symbolic vision, the LORD reached out His hand and touched Jeremiah’s mouth, saying that He had put His words in his mouth, as a sign that the prophet would deliver the word of the LORD.
Did you know? Jeremiah’s mission included both tearing down and uprooting, and building and planting; he was appointed over nations and kingdoms.
Did you know? Jeremiah saw an “almond branch,” and the vision involves a play on words: the almond tree symbolizes the LORD’s attentiveness to His word and His watchfulness to carry it out.

Did you know? The boiling pot tilted toward the north symbolizes disaster that will pour out from the north upon the people of the land, Jerusalem, and the cities of Judah, because they abandoned the LORD and worshiped other gods.
Did you know? So that he could stand against his opponents, Jeremiah was made like a fortified city, an iron pillar, and bronze walls; the LORD promised that they would not overcome him.
